story.title: Artificial entities make novelty verifiable
paragraphs: A correct answer about a new entity may come from memorization, from the supplied description, or from a guess prompted by a familiar name. ALCUNA controls for memorization by construction: its generator, KnowGen, creates artificial organisms by transforming entities in the Encyclopedia of Life (EOL) taxonomy, so every property traces back to a known operation.

Properties shared by the class are kept while selected attributes and relations change, so the questions stay biologically meaningful. This is a harder test than an arbitrary name with unrelated facts: the new entity resembles one the model already knows, so familiar knowledge can support reasoning or interfere with the new description.

mechanism.title: Each KnowGen operation fixes an expected answer
paragraphs: KnowGen starts from a parent entity and its siblings in the same class. Heredity keeps a parent property, variation perturbs a numeric value or swaps in a value from a related entity, extension adds a sibling's property, and dropout removes a parent property. Each operation fixes the expected answer to a question.

Differentiation questions target the varied and dropped properties. Asked for a lifespan that dropout removed, the correct answer is that it is unknown, even though the parent's lifespan is easy to recall. Association questions follow a relation from the artificial entity into existing knowledge and finish the chain with a fact absent from the new description.

Questions are filtered so that each model fully recalls the parent entity and every hop of a reasoning chain, and the intersection across models is used. A failure therefore points to combining facts, not to a missing prerequisite.

evidence.title: The bottleneck is linking new to existing knowledge
paragraphs: The context ablations show why separate ability scores matter. Supplying the chain entities raises association for all three open models, so the main problem is linking new and existing knowledge, not only multi-hop reasoning. Adding the parent entity instead lowers Vicuna's differentiation from 46.76 to 35.04: related context can supply a missing link or strengthen the wrong association.

Presentation also matters. All three open models score higher when the new entity is given as structured JSON than as natural-language text; ChatGLM's average falls to 20.54 with natural language. Success therefore depends partly on how new knowledge is communicated.

demo.title: Build Alcuna from Alpaca
demo.description: Switch KnowGen's operations on or off, then press Play to build the artificial entity one operation at a time. Each generated question lists the operations its expected answer depends on, and whether knowledge of the parent alone would answer it.

operations.heredity: Heredity keeps a parent property unchanged.
operations.variation: Variation perturbs a value: Gaussian noise for a number, a sibling of the related entity for a relation.
operations.dropout: Dropout removes a parent property from the new entity.
operations.extension: Extension adds a property sampled from a sibling of the parent.
